description: Report a problem you ran into while using a website or one of its tools (MCP, WebMCP or API), so the site's owners can fix it. Call this whenever you get stuck, are slowed down, or have to work around something on a website: information you couldn't find (e.g. shipping costs, return policy, sizes), a button or link that didn't work, a form that rejected valid input, a checkout or payment error, a confusing layout, a tool that failed or returned the wrong thing, no tool for what you needed, or anything that made the task harder than it should be. Report even if you eventually succeeded. Report each problem once, not again on every retry. If you found a way past it, say what worked, so other agents can try it. Be specific and factual: name the exact button or field involved and copy any error text word for word. Do not include personal data such as card numbers, passwords or addresses.

agent.description: Which agent you are: your product or framework and your model, e.g. "Claude in Chrome, Claude Sonnet 5.5" or "browser-use, GPT-5". Leave out if you don't know.

browser.description: Where the browser you are using runs: "user" = the person's own browser on their device; "cloud" = a hosted, remote or headless browser; "unknown" if you can't tell.

channel.description: How you were using the site: "browser" = clicking through its pages; "webmcp" = a WebMCP tool on the page; "mcp" = the site's MCP server; "api" = its API.

element.description: The exact button, link or form field involved, named as it appears on the page, e.g. "'Continue to payment' button" or "'ZIP code' field". Leave out if the problem wasn't about one element (e.g. information you couldn't find).

error_shown.description: Any error or warning the page showed, copied word for word. Write "none" if the page showed no error.

goal.description: What you were trying to accomplish, e.g. "Find the shipping cost to Canada before buying".

page_url.description: The full URL of the page where the problem happened, or of the MCP server or API endpoint if you were calling a tool.

severity.description: low = minor annoyance; medium = slowed you down; high = needed a workaround or guess; blocking = you could not complete the task.

tool.description: The name of the tool or API operation involved, e.g. "update_cart" or "POST /cart". If no tool existed for what you needed, name the tool you looked for. Leave out when you were using the site's pages.

what_i_tried.description: The concrete steps you took, in order, e.g. "Searched the product page, opened the FAQ, clicked 'Shipping' in the footer".

what_went_wrong.description: What actually happened and why it was a problem.

what_worked.description: If you got past the problem, the step that worked, e.g. "Reloading the page and clicking Continue again" or "Using the Guest checkout link under the sign-in form". Leave out if nothing worked.

name: report_friction
title: Report website friction
